title: Bring-Your-Own-HSM Onboarding, Rotation & Evidence Automation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook documents the recommended onboarding path for customers using Bring-Your-Own-HSM (BYO-HSM) with Redwood, the operational rotation cadence and steps for managed key versions, and the evidence automation pattern that produces SIEM-ready events and auditable artifacts. It ties RBAC v2 role checks to each action and prescribes how to collect and store cryptographic attestations for compliance reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to BYO-HSM and customer-managed HSM appliances (cloud HSM + on-prem HSM via gateway).
- Covers initial onboarding handshake, key import/escrow options, periodic rotation, emergency revocation, and evidence export for SIEM and GRC teams.
- Does NOT replace tenant-level KMS service behavior; this is an integration/operational playbook for when custody is delegated.

High-level goals:
1) Ensure every cryptographic operation has: a) RBACv2 action-authorizer, b) cryptographic attestation blob, c) SIEM event with consistent schema.
2) Keep rotation windows auditable and automatic where possible.
3) Minimize downtime during key roll while preserving deterministic audit trails.

Key definitions (short):
- HSM: Hardware Security Module under customer control.
- BYO-HSM Gateway: Redwood’s trusted proxy that mediates KMS API calls to customer HSM via mutually-authenticated TLS.
- Escrow: Optional encrypted backup of keys (only for allowed key types).
- Attestation: HSM-signed statement (certificate or signed statement) verifying key origin and properties.
- Evidence package: Timebound bundle (log + attestation + request/response) stored in evidence store for audits.

Onboarding flow (step-by-step):
1) Pre-onboarding checklist (customer): HSM model, firmware version, supported algorithms, management-plane access, FIPS/HSM certs.
2) Legal & Configuration: sign BYO addendum, exchange PKI materials (Redwood gateway certs + HSM management certs), agree on escrow policy (allowed/not-allowed).
3) RBAC v2 mapping setup: create the following Redwood roles for the tenant: 
   - key-admin (can import, rotate, revoke keys)
   - key-operator (can perform encrypt/decrypt via API)
   - key-auditor (read-only: list keys, versions, fetch evidence)
   - key-incident (emergency revoke + rotate)
   Map customer SSO groups to these roles. Store mapping in tenant metadata.
4) Gateway provisioning: deploy BYO-HSM gateway in tenant network or enable Redwood’s connector; exchange mTLS client certs.
5) Test vectors & attestation capture: import a non-production test key, run sample encrypt/decrypt, capture HSM attestation and gateway logs. Verify evidence package pipeline: evidence_id created, SIEM event emitted, evidence stored in evidence-bucket.
6) Sign-off: security & compliance perform verification using the evidence package and attestation.

Rotation policy (recommended baseline):
- Symmetric data keys: rotate every 90 days by default; strong customers may choose 30 days.
- Master wrapping keys (HSM root keys): rotate only when supported by HSM via key-subkey rotation pattern (i.e., create new wrapping key, rewrap active keys).
- Key versioning: always keep previous N=3 versions available for decrypting replays; mark older versions as archived.
- Automatic vs manual: support automatic rotation for tenant-managed scripts invoked by Redwood orchestration. Automatic rotations must run a pre-rotation dry-run.

Rotation orchestration sequence (detailed):
1) Pre-rotation checks (RBAC enforcement: key-admin required): health checks of HSM, gateway heartbeat, pending operations, consumer usage patterns.
2) Create new key version on HSM (or request new wrapped key from customer HSM).
3) Rewrap/reencrypt metadata: update envelope keys for objects created since last rotation — use background rewrap worker with idempotent checkpoints.
4) Warm routing: start routing a percentage (canary 5-10%) of decrypt requests to new version; monitor for errors for 1–3h depending on SLA.
5) Promote new version to primary after canary success. Emit rotation-complete evidence package.
6) Soft-deprecate older versions; schedule archival after retention window.

Emergency revoke & rollback:
- Triggerers: compromise report, HSM compromise flag, lost attestation, immediate SLA breach.
- Authorized roles: key-incident OR external signed request from customer SRE (validated by RBACv2 + signed JWT).
- Steps: 1) Quarantine key: deny API ops via RBAC flag and gateway ACL. 2) Emit an immediate SIEM-critical event. 3) If possible, create new key material and rewrap; otherwise switch to fallback wrapping with Redwood-managed ephemeral key. 4) Create an incident evidence bundle and store with higher retention label.

Evidence automation pattern (engine):
- Sources to capture: gateway access logs, HSM attestation artifacts (signed certs or signed statements), KMS API request/response payloads, RBAC decision logs (who allowed/denied), and orchestration events (rotation-start/complete).
- Evidence object model (flat fields for SIEM export):
   evidence_id: <uuid>,
   event_time: <ISO8601>,
   tenant_id: <string>,
   actor_subject: <principal_id or service>,
   actor_role: <rbac_role>,
   action: <import|rotate|revoke|decrypt|encrypt|rewrap>,
   key_id: <tenant:keyname>,
   key_version: <v2>,
   hsm_certificate_serial: <serial|null>,
   attestation_present: <true|false>,
   attestation_sha256: <hex>,
   request_id: <uuid>,
   outcome: <success|failure>,
   error_code: <optional>,
   evidence_bucket_path: <s3://.../evidence_id.tar.gz>,
   siem_event_type: "redwood.key.operation",
   severity: <informational|warning|critical>,
   sla_ms: <elapsed_ms>,
   notes: <free text>
- Evidence pipeline: events are generated by gateway + KMS proxy -> event normalizer -> signer (adds orchestration signature) -> archived bundle (tar.gz) -> metadata record written to evidence DB and SIEM exporter pushes normalized json to SIEM via HTTPS with HMAC auth.

SIEM export schema considerations:
- Use flat key/value pairs to simplify correlation with existing SIEM dashboards. Avoid deeply nested JSON to preserve event indexing performance.
- Recommend mapping fields: tenant_id, key_id, key_version, action, actor_subject, actor_role, request_id, evidence_id, attestation_sha256, hsm_certificate_serial, outcome, severity, event_time.
- Include a "composite_search_key": tenant_id + key_id + request_id to help triage.
- For high-volume tenants, sample non-error events at 1% for long-term retention, but always forward 100% of error/warning/critical events.

RBAC v2 integration notes:
- Every principal action passes through the RBAC v2 evaluator. Ensure evaluator logs include: principal_id, role_bindings_checked, policy_version, decision (allow/deny), reason_code, policy_match_path. These logs become part of the evidence bundle.
- Role separation: key-admin cannot sign audit attestations, key-auditor cannot trigger rotation. Enforce via explicit policy denies.

Post-rotation evidence package (contents):
- rotation-manifest.json (flat fields as above),
- gateway.log (request/response slices with timestamps),
- hsm-attestation.pem (signed by HSM),
- orchestration-signature.sig (signed by Redwood orchestration signing key),
- replay-checksum.txt (list of rewrap operations and checksums),
- compliance-checks.txt (automated rules run result).

Retention & archival:
- Standard evidence retention: 2 years for typical keys.
- High-security tenants: configurable to 7+ years.
- Evidence storage encryption: evidence-bucket encrypted with tenant-wrapped key; access controlled by RBACv2 key-auditor/forensics roles.
- Export for eDiscovery: on request, provide signed evidence bundle with integrity checksum.

Attestation validation checklist (for auditors):
- Verify HSM model and firmware match onboarding record.
- Validate attestation signature chain to recognized root.
- Confirm attestation contains key attributes (algorithm, bitlength, usage flags).
- Confirm attestation timestamp is within expected window of operation.

Operational runbook snippets (commands & checks):
- Verify gateway health: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <gw-token>' https://gateway.tenant.example/v1/health
- Fetch evidence manifest: aws s3 cp s3://evidence-bucket/<evidence_id>/rotation-manifest.json -
- Validate attestation SHA: openssl dgst -sha256 hsm-attestation.pem
- Produce SIEM sample payload (minimal): {
  "siem_event_type": "redwood.key.operation",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "event_time": "2024-11-01T12:23:45Z",
  "action": "rotate",
  "key_id": "tenant-123:data-key-01",
  "key_version": "v3",
  "actor_subject": "user:m.gonzalez@redwood.example",
  "actor_role": "key-admin",
  "evidence_id": "evid-7f3c9a2b",
  "attestation_sha256": "a3b1...",
  "outcome": "success"
}

Testing & verification matrix:
- Dry-run rotation: run via orchestration flag --dry-run, confirm no change to primary, verify evidence bundle generated with "dry-run": true.
- Replay test: re-execute an archived evidence bundle against a dedicated test HSM to ensure artifacts reproduce the operation.
- Chaos test: simulate gateway network partition and verify fallback to Redwood-wrapped ephemeral key path while generating incident evidence.

Audit and reporting:
- Weekly digest: counts of rotation events, revocations, failed attestation validations, and critical SIEM events. Export to compliance slack channel and Confluence page summary.
- Quarterly audit: hand off evidence bundles for a sample of rotations (3 per quarter) to the GRC team for manual review.

Open questions / future enhancements:
- Support for HSM-attested key rotation proofs that include TPM-style PCR history (customer ask).
- Automating escrow requests with time-limited access tokens for on-demand eDiscovery.
- Cross-cloud HSM federation and single-slate attestation aggregation.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for on-call (short):
- If an HSM attestation fails: mark key as "attestation-failed" and notify key-incident role.
- If unexpected decrypt failures spike >1% for 10m: switch canary routing back and trigger rotated rollback action.
- For confirmed compromise: follow Emergency revoke steps and label evidence with incident severity=critical.

Appendix B — Example RBAC binding snippet (pseudo):
- tenant: tenant-123
  bindings:
    - role: key-admin
      subjects: [group:tenant-123-sre]
    - role: key-operator
      subjects: [service:payments, group:tenant-123-apps]
    - role: key-auditor
      subjects: [group:tenant-123-compliance]

Notes and provenance: This was assembled from product integration experiments (Q2 2024), customer onboarding retros, and compliance requests from two enterprise pilots. Reviewers: Arjun Patel (security eng), Leah Kim (compliance), Tomás Rivera (platform ops).
